root_cause.text: In the `ad3552r_hs_write_data_source` function of the IIO DAC driver, an out-of-bounds stack write occurs because the code uses the user-provided `count` parameter instead of the actual bytes copied returned by `simple_write_to_buffer()` to index the null terminator, exceeding the fixed 64-byte buffer limit when input size exceeds capacity.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `buf[count] = '\0'` with `buf[ret] = '\0'` and adds a check `if (count >= sizeof(buf))`, while the CVE description explicitly states that if `count` exceeds the buffer size (e.g., 128 bytes vs 64-byte buffer), writing `buf[count] = '\0'` causes an out-of-bounds write on the stack.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement writes a null terminator at index 'ret' (the number of bytes copied from user space via simple_write_to_buffer()) into a fixed 64-byte stack buffer. When user-provided count exceeds the buffer capacity, 'ret' can exceed 63, causing an out-of-bounds stack write. The fix should validate that ret < sizeof(buf) before writing the null terminator.
